title: What should you confirm before same-day office catering?
body_markdown:
Before arranging same-day office catering, confirm that the caterer has accepted your order, the food can reach your actual serving point before lunch, and the menu covers your headcount and dietary requirements. Your same day office catering checklist should also cover building access, service equipment, staffing, the full quotation and a named handover contact. An enquiry alone is not a confirmed booking.


**TL;DR**

- Use this same day office catering checklist to confirm acceptance, lunch timing, dietary requirements and building access.
- Separate the delivery window from the time food must be ready to serve.
- Choose individual meals, a shared buffet or staffed service around your office facilities and meeting schedule.
- myCHEF provides corporate event catering; request explicit confirmation before treating a same-day enquiry as booked.


## What should you confirm before same-day office catering?

**Confirm the complete delivery and service plan, not just the menu.** A lunch order is ready to approve when the caterer and your office contact agree on what is arriving, where it is going and who takes responsibility at handover.

Use these 7 checks before authorising the order:

1. **Order acceptance:** written confirmation of the agreed scope, rather than an acknowledgement of your enquiry.
2. **Headcount:** the total number eating, including visitors, and a separate breakdown of dietary meals.
3. **Menu:** named dishes, portion basis, dietary information and agreed substitutions.
4. **Timing:** the delivery window, setup requirements and the time lunch must be ready.
5. **Access:** the building, entrance, floor, reception process and route to the serving point.
6. **Service scope:** packaging, equipment, staffing, clearing and collection responsibilities.
7. **Commercial approval:** the complete quotation, payment requirements and terms for changes or cancellation.

For shared buildings, the guide to [connecting office facilities management to lunch catering](https://www.mychef.ae/blog/how-to-connect-office-facilities-management-to-lunch-catering) addresses the coordination behind that handover.

Do not leave an unresolved item buried in a message thread. Ask for a revised summary that everyone can approve.

## Why does the handover matter as much as the food?

A delivery reaching the building is not the same as lunch being ready in your meeting room. Reception, access checks, unloading and arranging food are separate parts of the plan.

Work backwards from the moment guests need to eat. Tell the caterer whether lunch follows a presentation, sits inside a short meeting break or remains accessible while colleagues eat at different times.

**Give the caterer a ready-to-serve deadline, not just a preferred arrival time.** Ask the caterer to propose the delivery window needed to meet it, then check that the building can accommodate that plan.

Assign 2 named contacts: an office receiver and a catering contact. Both should have the final brief and a direct way to reach each other. Reception can help with access, but do not assume reception has agreed to check quantities or set out lunch.

## Which service format fits your office lunch?

Choose the format before approving dishes. It determines how much space, equipment and coordination the office needs.

These are planning options to discuss with a caterer, not a statement that every format can be arranged at short notice.

| Format | Best for | Practical advantage | Limitation to resolve |
|---|---|---|---|
| Individually packed meals | Desk lunches and staggered breaks | Meals can be allocated to named recipients | Dietary labels, packaging waste and distribution still need an owner |
| Shared buffet | Teams eating together in a designated area | Guests can select from shared dishes | Requires serving space, utensils and an agreed food-holding plan |
| Staffed service | Hosted meetings and corporate occasions | Service responsibilities can sit with an agreed team | Staffing, access, setup and clearing must be explicitly included |

### Individually packed meals: best for staggered breaks

Choose individual meals when colleagues eat in different rooms or at different times. Ask how each meal will be identified and whether the packaging includes everything needed to eat it.

The trade-off is distribution. Someone still needs to match dietary meals to recipients and deal with packaging afterwards. A box marked only with a dish name does not settle every dietary question.

### Shared buffet: best for a defined lunch area

Choose a shared buffet when your team can gather around an agreed serving point. Confirm the table position, serving utensils and how dishes will be maintained until service.

A buffet transfers practical tasks to the office unless those tasks are included in the booking. Do not assume delivery includes arranging dishes, monitoring the serving area or clearing it afterwards.

### Staffed service: best for hosted occasions

Consider staffed service when lunch is part of a client meeting or corporate event and you need agreed service responsibilities. Specify which tasks the staff should handle, rather than requesting staff without a job description.

The limitation is a broader operational brief. Confirm personnel access, working space, equipment, service timing and the point at which the team finishes.

## What should the dietary and menu confirmation include?

Send dietary requirements before approving the menu. Separate allergies from preferences, and describe each requirement clearly rather than grouping everything under a general request for healthy food.

Ask the caterer to confirm which dishes suit each requirement and how the relevant meals will be identified. For an allergy, request specific information about ingredients and cross-contact controls; a vegetarian or gluten-free label alone does not answer that question.

Your menu approval should cover:

- **Dish details:** the actual dishes and accompaniments being supplied.
- **Portion basis:** whether the proposal provides individual meals or shared quantities for the confirmed headcount.
- **Dietary allocation:** which meals are intended for which requirements.
- **Substitutions:** which changes require your approval before preparation or dispatch.
- **Drinks and extras:** whether beverages, desserts, sauces and condiments are included.

If halal suitability is required, state that requirement and request confirmation for the proposed menu. Do not infer suitability from a cuisine name.

**Never accept an unapproved substitution for a dietary meal.** If the caterer cannot confirm that a replacement meets the stated requirement, agree a different suitable option before approving it.

## What building and kitchen details should you send?

Give the caterer the full address and the route from arrival to handover. A map location does not explain which entrance accepts deliveries or how food reaches your floor.

Confirm these details with your office or building team:

- **Building access:** delivery entrance, reception instructions and any advance information the building requests.
- **Handover point:** floor, room and the person authorised to receive the order.
- **Serving space:** a clear table or counter, with its location agreed in advance.
- **Equipment:** plates, cutlery, napkins, serving utensils and any required holding equipment.
- **Clearing:** responsibility for food containers, waste and equipment collection.


![Office catering handover checklist covering access, serving space, equipment and clearing](https://gwvckixiegkllthleuyt.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/workspace-article-images-public/7adc401b-1956-457f-b430-acf85633b9ed/body-25a5b9b651012a9f84d75a1c2cb3edfc.jpg)

*Agree the route to the serving point and assign the tasks around it before delivery.*


Describe the facilities accurately. If your office has a pantry but no cooking equipment, say so. If refrigeration, reheating or hot holding is needed, ask the caterer what arrangements the proposed menu requires and confirm who supplies them.

Do not agree to on-site preparation without explaining the available workspace. The caterer needs to assess the proposed service against the actual facilities, not an assumption about a typical office kitchen.

## Why does same-day catering feasibility vary?

A same-day request needs an explicit operational answer. These factors belong in that discussion:

- **Requested menu:** ask which dishes the caterer can commit to for your deadline rather than assuming the full menu applies.
- **Headcount:** confirm the number of meals and whether additions can be accepted after approval.
- **Dietary complexity:** establish which requirements the caterer can accommodate and document clearly.
- **Delivery and access:** account for the route into the building and movement to the serving area.
- **Service format:** distinguish food delivery from setup, staffed service and clearing.
- **Approval process:** tell the caterer whether a purchase order, supplier registration or internal payment approval is required.

Ask what must change if the original brief cannot be accepted. A revised menu, different format or adjusted serving plan is a new proposal, not automatic permission to proceed.

**Approve only a plan your office can actually receive and serve.** A simpler confirmed arrangement is preferable to an elaborate request with unresolved responsibilities.

## What should you check in the quotation?

Read the quotation against the operational brief. A total without a clear scope does not tell you whether the lunch is fully arranged.

Confirm whether the quotation covers delivery, dietary meals, service equipment, staffing, setup, clearing and any applicable charges. Ask whether equipment must be returned or collected, and who coordinates that collection.

Check the payment deadline and the point at which the caterer considers the order confirmed. Ask for the terms governing headcount changes, menu changes, delays and cancellation before authorising payment.

For a company order, provide the correct billing entity and purchase-order details at the start. Keep the payment approver involved so an internal authorisation step does not remain unresolved after the menu is agreed.

## What should you send in your first enquiry?

Send 1 consolidated brief rather than several incomplete messages. It gives the caterer a clear request to accept, revise or decline.

Use this copy-and-complete checklist:

- **Date and location:** office address, building, floor and room.
- **Lunch timing:** when food must be ready and any fixed meeting break.
- **Guest count:** total diners, visitors and separately identified dietary requirements.
- **Service required:** individual meals, shared buffet or staffed service.
- **Menu preferences:** preferred dishes or cuisines, with acceptable alternatives.
- **Facilities:** serving space, pantry equipment and access arrangements.
- **Commercial details:** budget brief, billing requirements and approval contact.
- **Handover details:** receiver's name and direct contact information.

**myCHEF corporate catering suits businesses seeking a service shaped around their event brief.** Include the same operational details in your enquiry, and request explicit acceptance of the proposed same-day schedule. Tailored catering is not a promise that an unconfirmed short-notice request has been accepted.

Keep the final approved version together. If your headcount or timing changes, ask the caterer to acknowledge the amendment rather than assuming a later message has replaced the original instructions.

## FAQ


**Can I assume my same-day office catering order is booked after sending an enquiry?**

No. Request written acceptance of the menu, headcount, timing, location and service scope, and complete any stated confirmation requirements. An enquiry acknowledgement is not the same as an accepted order.

**What time should I ask office catering to arrive?**

Give the caterer your ready-to-serve deadline and ask for a delivery window that allows for access and setup. Confirm that the office receiver and building arrangements support that window.

**Are individual lunch boxes better than a buffet for an office?**

Individual meals suit staggered breaks, while a shared buffet suits a team eating in an agreed lunch area. Choose around your schedule, dietary allocation, serving space and clearing responsibilities.

**Can I include food allergies in a same-day catering request?**

State every allergy before approving the menu and request explicit confirmation of suitable dishes and cross-contact controls. Do not treat a general dietary label as an allergy assurance.

**Does office catering include plates, serving staff and cleanup?**

Include plates, staffing and cleanup only when the written scope confirms them. Ask separately about cutlery, serving utensils, setup, waste removal and equipment collection.

**What should I send myCHEF for a same-day corporate catering enquiry?**

Send myCHEF the date, Dubai location, guest count, ready-to-serve time and service required. Add dietary requirements, building access, facilities and billing details so the proposed arrangement can be assessed.

Wait until the catering arrangement is confirmed before telling colleagues exactly what will be served and when. Share the approved dietary collection instructions with the receiver, not just the person who placed the order.

For a tailored myCHEF corporate catering enquiry, send your **date, location, guest count and service required**, together with the time lunch must be ready. Ask for confirmation of the menu, handover plan and service scope before treating the booking as agreed.
